name: Execution Quality Check
description: Standardized SEC Rule 605 execution-quality reports for August and September 2026, made comparable: reporter-by-reporter spread, price-improvement and execution statistics for exchanges and broker-dealers, plus a per-symbol explorer and a coverage ledger of who has and has not published — exactly as filed, with hash receipts and documented data-quality notes. September is the default month. August stays selectable.
data_source: Amended-format SEC Rule 605 reports for August and September 2026 from the exchanges' own sites (Cboe, IEX, MIAX, MEMX, Nasdaq), the shared Download Site host that NYSE, 24X and most broker-dealers use, and firm-hosted Download Sites: detailed 55-field pipe-delimited files + OES summary CSVs, fetched with SHA-256 receipts. Each month is built from that month's files only.
records: September 2026 (default): 170 reporters; 18,052,735 detailed rows; 14,715 symbols; 4,047 published summary rows; 153 of 223 FINRA-registered firms in the build. August 2026 remains selectable: 169 reporters; 17,714,825 detailed rows; 14,534 symbols; 4,127 summary rows; 151 of 223. On 2026-11-03 ETMM, MSSB, SOHW, and FFSI had replaced their August files. GSCO, GSBD, and SGMT returned HTTP 403, and FTBR failed TLS verification; those four August rows are still the 2026-10-03 capture and were not withdrawn. They are absent from September, not carried forward. Park Avenue Securities verified 2026-10-21 as PAWM (formerly PASC). Moomoo (FUTM) was HTTP 404 in August and is in the September build.
detail: Reporter comparison by order size band × stock universe × order type across the published statistics (price improvement, at-quote rate, effective/quoted spread, EFQ, realized spreads), sortable and filterable by reporter type; per-symbol explorer comparing every reporter that filed records for a stock; coverage ledger of every FINRA-registered reporter (in the build / registered with no file located / Download Site not retrieved) with probe evidence; method page with file receipts, per-reporter unit checks, sanity filters and filing anomalies found during the build.
asymmetry: Brokers and venues benefit when execution quality stays fragmented across hundreds of separate monthly downloads; the standardized format exists so executions can be compared, but nobody has assembled the comparison. Investors comparing venues — or checking whether their fills are measurably worse than the market's — need the portage layer: many Download Sites → searchable, comparable tables.
pipeline_note: Header-driven parsing of the 55-field detailed files, parallel per reporter; executed shares = executed at the reporter + executed away (price-improvement share checked against the published S&P 500/other bracket: 857/857 reporter-size cells on the 2026-10-18 re-fetch); EFQ units detected per reporter from the filed rows and cross-checked against the summary (6 reporters write percent-points and are normalized); headerless, gz, nested-zip and alias-code filings handled and recorded; conservative row-sanity filters for weighted statistics only (exclusions counted per reporter); notional fields excluded due to sentinel-value anomalies; nil, IOC-only and summary-less reporters kept and labeled; 256-way symbol shards by a Python/JS FNV-1a pair with an all-symbols parity test; 2026-10-04 post-deadline harvest build, Playwright browser smoke over the staged site; static, no backend. Re-fetched 2026-10-18: CHAS, JANY, JANM, SFBD, SFMM, JNST and JSJX had replaced their August files, and the page shows those current files (first-filed bytes kept with the source build). FUTM returned HTTP 404 and is not shown. On 2026-10-23, applied CODX detailed and MLWM detailed/summary replacements found by the full-source freshness checker; prior working files retained. On 2026-11-03, applied ETMM, MSSB, SOHW, and FFSI replacements from the same checker. GSCO, GSBD, and SGMT returned HTTP 403, and FTBR failed TLS verification; those stored files were not replaced. September 2026 built 2026-11-03 from that month's own receipts (shared-host harvest, firm pages, FINRA sweep); IEX's September detailed file is one nested zip, read with the existing one-level unwrap. Default month is September. August stays selectable, including the four files that could not be reread.
